verse_notes.note: Names 78–84 close the war with Bhaṇḍāsura: the obstacle-yantra (78), the counter-missiles (79), the ten avatāras (80), the Pāśupata and Kāmeśvara missiles (81–82), the gods' praise (83) and the revival of Kāma (84). Each half-śloka here is a single name.
Name 80 ends in -iḥ, not -ā: its last member ākṛti is a feminine i-stem.
Name 82: Śūnyaka is the name of Bhaṇḍa's city, and sa-bhaṇḍāsura means 'together with Bhaṇḍāsura'. Name 83: Mahendra is Indra and Upendra is Viṣṇu.
Name 84 completes the Bhaṇḍa episode. Name 85 begins the subtle form (sūkṣma-rūpa): the three kūṭas of the Pañcadaśī as Her body (85–89).
Name 86 keeps the visarga of adhaḥ before k (kaṇṭhādhaḥ-kaṭi); in name 87 the same adhas appears as adho- before bh.
Four names in this śloka. From name 90 the hymn turns to kula and the ascent of kuṇḍalinī (to name 111).

Kula and its opposite are paired: Kaulinī (94) and Akulā (96, beginning with the negative a-); the Kaula and Samaya paths (93, 97–98). In 93 and 97, -āntasthā is best divided antar + sthā ('abiding within').
Names 99–104 trace kuṇḍalinī's ascent in order: mūlādhāra, the knot of Brahmā, maṇipūra, the knot of Viṣṇu, ājñā, the knot of Rudra. Name 101 is maṇipūra-antar-uditā; maṇipūra is one cakra name.
Name 106: sudhāsāra is best divided sudhā + āsāra 'downpour of nectar'.
Name 109 is read महासक्तिः with dental s (maha 'festival' + āsakti 'attachment'); many printed editions have महाशक्तिः 'the great power'. Name 107 is also found as taṭillatā.

report.summary: Checked all 34 names of ślokas 31–40 against text.json (the end of the Bhaṇḍāsura war, the three kūṭas of the subtle form, and the kula/kuṇḍalinī section): sandhi at every member and visible prefix junction, layered samāsa analysis with pausa vigrahas, and each meaning against that analysis. Several members were misidentified in the old splits: 82 śūnyakā is Bhaṇḍa's city Śūnyaka, not 'void'; 106 is sudhā + āsāra 'downpour', not sāra 'essence'; 109 has dental s (āsakti 'attachment'), not śakti 'power'; 101 cut through maṇipūra. Name 83's meaning (Mahendra glossed as Śiva) was replaced and 86's truncated meaning completed. No problem was found in the Sanskrit; no external sandhi joins names in these ślokas.
